newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Moody's raises Argentine outlook to positive-paper.
newsitem.headline: Moody's raises Argentine outlook to positive-paper.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc has raised the outlook on Argentina's debt rating to "positive" from "stable," Argentine business daily El Cronista reported Thursday.
"Although the country faces a large financing requirement in the medium-term, ample international liquidity improves the chances of refinancing," El Cronista quoted Moody's as saying.
Moody's rates Argentine foreign-currency debt B1.
The rating agency said improvements in the country's tax system should reduce the necessity for new increases in foreign debt, according to the business daily.

"Popular expectations will weigh heavily on politicians in the next three years, because of the high jobless rate, but it is likely the voters will support the candidates they perceive as guaranteeing stability," El Cronista quoted Moody's as saying.

Standard & Poor's Corp recently upgraded Argentina's foreign-currency debt rating to BB from BB-minus, but Moody's has been reluctant to do the same because of Argentina's relatively high external debt burden, especially when measured as a percentage of exports.
